summary: The assessee, a Hindu undivided family, was assessed to income tax under the Income tax Act, 1922, for the assessment year 1957 58. The assessee claimed that the income of the assessee 's family was not taxable under the Act. The Income tax Officer, however, rejected the claim of the assessee for the assessment years 1957 58 and 1958 58. The Appellate Assistant Commissioner held that the income was taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1921, and that the income could not be assessed under the Act, and that, therefore, the income was liable to be assessed under section 10(2)(xv) of the Act. In appeal to this Court, it was contended on behalf of the assessee that the income in question was taxable under section 10 of the Act and that the assessee was liable to pay income tax under section 10, and that section 10(1)(xv) was not applicable to the case. Dismissing the appeal, HELD: (1) The income in question is taxable under the head "Profits and gains of business or profession" of the assessee. The income in the case of a Hindu undivided Hindu undivided family is taxable under section 2(1)(iii) of the Income tax (Amendment) Act, 1961. The income is taxable under that Act. The income of the Hindu undivided family in the case is taxable under Section 10(1) of the Indian Income tax Act. The assessee is liable to pay tax under the Act on the income of his family. [860 G H] (2) The income of a Hindu Hindu undivided family which is taxable under this Act is taxable under s.10(1) (xv) of that Act. [861 G] (3) The income is not taxable under section 9(1)(vii) of the 1922 Act. The tax is payable under the Act and the income is taxable. [862 G] (4) The income under the head 'Profits and losses ' of the Hindu family is taxable. The income under section 10 is taxable under any other head. The income from the income of a family is taxable in the hands of the assessee and the income from the business of the family is taxable only under the head. [863 G H]
